title: Regulatory Evidence Assembler and Verification Manifest
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight service and Console UX that assembles timebound, zone-aware evidence bundles (manifests) for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls. Each manifest must map raw artifacts (logs, DB snapshots, config exports, KMS audit entries) to control IDs, include provenance (timestamp, region tag, collector id), attest cryptographic integrity (signatures or content hashes), and expose an API for on-demand retrieval and scheduled exports to customer-specified storage (S3/GCS) with WORM options.
background: Customers and auditors ask for concise, verifiable bundles that prove controls were in effect during an audit window. Existing evidence endpoints return loose artifacts without consistent mapping, making auditor review manual and slow. This initiative reduces manual auditor effort and supports private/Dedicated customers who must demonstrate region-bound custody and retention enforcement.
goals: Produce a manifest format (JSON-LD) that maps artifacts to standard control IDs (SOC2 CC/ISO 27001 Annex A refs).
Implement an Evidence Assembler service that can build manifests for arbitrary time windows and regions on demand.
Surface a Console flow: select controls, window, residency constraint -> preview manifest -> export to cloud storage with immutable retention flag.
Add cryptographic integrity markers (SHA-256 hashes + signature using Redwood signing key or customer KMS) for each artifact reference.
Provide an API endpoint for auditors to fetch manifests and artifact verification data programmatically.
Instrument metrics: manifest generation latency, size, success rate, and downstream export durability.
Ensure the feature works for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes with clear RBAC and audit logs.
tasks: Design manifest schema and mapping table between internal telemetry/events and control IDs (PM + Security + Research workshop).
Prototype Assembler service: query collectors, attach provenance metadata, compute hashes, assemble manifest.
Add signing integration: option to sign with Redwood key or customer KMS-managed key (design HSM/KMS flow).
Console UX: design screens for selection, preview, and export flows + retention tag selector.
Export worker: S3/GCS exporter supporting object lock/WORM and customizable retention TTL.
Backfill test data and create sample manifests for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scoping exercises.
E2E QA: auditor review session and internal checklist runbook.
Docs: PRD + Console help + API reference + migration notes for Dedicated/Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema approved by Security and Compliance (documented JSON schema file link).
Assembler builds manifests for requested window with >99% artifact inclusion coverage for supported collectors.
Each manifest includes per-artifact provenance (collector id, timestamp, region, checksum) and top-level signature.
Exported bundles land in target storage with retention/lock metadata set; verification script can validate all checksums and signature.
Console flow passes usability review with Solutions Engineering and at least two pilot customers signed up.
API responds within SLO (95th percentile < 8s for 30-day window) and instruments metrics in Console.
Security review completed and threat model updated; no critical findings outstanding.
tradeoffs_considered: Strongly coupling manifests to a single schema simplifies auditor automation but reduces flexibility for future control frameworks. We will version manifests and support layered extensions. Using Redwood signing key eases rollout; KMS signing provides customer-segregated trust but requires KMS work and support matrix for Dedicated/Private environments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): implement read-only assembler for hosted with Redwood signing; pilot with 2 customers. Phase 2: add export worker + Console UI + retention flags. Phase 3: KMS signing and Dedicated/Private compatibility. Each phase has a 2-week pilot and an auditor feedback session.
notes: Collectors to prioritize: access logs, key rotation events, config snapshots, autoscaling and routing policies. Need alignment with Legal on export encryption-at-rest expectations for cross-border bundles. Schedule a compliance sync with pilot customers in Week 1 of Cycle 2026-W09.
